goal: A 5-minute playable vertical slice that captures the core fantasy of Palworld: a beautiful third-person world, charming creatures, meaningful interaction, and believable creature behaviour.
bar: The real Palworld. A fresh critic is shown our capture beside an official Palworld frame — same shot type, same resolution, same format, labels stripped, order shuffled — and asked which one is the shipped commercial game. We are done when critics stop reliably picking correctly.
currentState:
Round 12 is the widest round yet: six builders on disjoint directories. Three are closing the gaps the r11 blind critic named — the empty near field, the flat dusk frame, and creatures that read as 'lit from every direction equally'. Three are building two new mechanics the user asked for: throw-to-capture Bond Spheres, and a GTA-feel firearms module.

The near field has already changed character — the bare grass carpet is now layered clumps, flowers and foreground detail — at 250 draws / 1.74M triangles against a 300 / 2.2M budget. All six systems boot together and capture cleanly.
pickRate: 0% across r08, r10 and r11 — a blind critic has identified our frame as the in-dev one in 15 of 15 pairs. In r11 every verdict came back at confidence 5. Art direction, judged as a separate question, went 1 of 5 to us (the creature group: 'B's frame is calm and legible... as a picture, B is the better-composed one').

metrics.caption: Objective guardrails, measured with tools/measure.py against the real reference frames. Not the bar — a critic's eye is — but they stop arguments about whether a change helped. Two bands were corrected in r08 after being measured from the reference rather than invented.

rows.name: cast shadows contribute to image
rows.note: Shadows now render correctly — proven visually and by a max per-pixel delta of 96/255 where casters exist. The low mean is now a CONTENT failure, not a rendering one: nothing occupies the near field to cast.

openGaps: NOTHING MEETS THE GROUND. The r11 critic's decisive cue in the creature-group pair: our foreground bush is 'an icosphere with berries as separate spheres stuck to it, sitting on the grass with no contact shadow and no ambient occlusion at the ground line. It doesn't sit in the world, it sits on top of the image.' The same defect names the creature portrait — a hard black elliptical blob decal instead of an occlusion gradient.

CREATURES ARE LIT FROM EVERY DIRECTION EQUALLY. 'The underside of the creature is the same value as the top.' Prime suspect is the fur wrap term (0.60), which remaps a fully back-facing surface up to 0.375 and flattens a sphere into a disc. The designs themselves were praised — 'it's the rendering that fails it, not the design.'

DUSK IS A DAY RENDER WITH THE EXPOSURE PULLED. Independently reached by the r11 critic and by the guardrails from the other side: ground/sky 0.99 against the reference plate's 1.27. 'A night scene with no light sources in it. The fireflies are unlit point sprites contributing nothing... the brightest thing in frame is the HUD.'

THE FIRST 25 METRES ARE EMPTY. Per-band shadow coverage down the over-shoulder frame reads 0.011 / 0.042 / 0.186 / 0.050 / 0.000 / 0.027 from sky to nearest. Mid-distance works; the near meadow is bare grass carpet. Same root cause as the flat palette (337 colours against a 420-1100 band) and the low local contrast (5.06 against real plates at 8.06-9.87).

OUR POST IS NOT READING AT ALL. 'Uniformly, mercilessly sharp from the grass blade at the camera to the peak on the horizon', 'no aerial perspective — the terrain collapses into a stack of flat cutouts'. We ship FogExp2, aerial-perspective materials AND a DOF pass, so this is a strength-of-effect problem, not a missing feature — which is worse, because it means we are paying for all three and reading as if we had none.

UNTEXTURED GREY PROPS SIT AT FOCAL POINTS. The stone arch 'reads as unshipped greybox: a placeholder blockout that never got a material pass, placed exactly where the eye lands'. Contrast the reference: 'cliff faces carry layered strata with moss accumulating only on upward-facing ledges — a material that knows which way gravity points.' The arch is a landmark in world/index.js and is not yet assigned.

TERRAIN IS ONE MATERIAL AT ONE SCALE. The same ground mottle and grass card run from camera to horizon with no density falloff, no dirt paths, no rock or sand transitions. 'Real ground tells you where people walk.' Not yet assigned.
Reference gap: only 1 of 17 official stills is early-game peaceful exploration, so interaction_feed has no honest comp.
Reference gap: the trailer never shows a creature noticing an approaching player, so behaviour_approach is graded against the 12 written criteria.

rounds.title: Near field, dusk, creature shading — and two new mechanics
rounds.summary:
Split across two fronts. The first three builders answer the r11 critic directly: it ranked 'nothing in the in-dev world casts or receives light locally' as the single biggest gap, ahead of atmospheric depth and terrain variety. The other three add throw-to-capture and firearms.

The design decision that makes the two new mechanics one feature rather than two: catch chance is read straight off the trust the berries bought. Feeding is not made obsolete by the sphere — it is what makes the sphere work. And the guns exist to weaken and stagger a creature so a sphere will hold it, which is the only framing in which firearms belong in a game about befriending things. There is no death anywhere in the build.
improvements: Bond Spheres: aim arc showing the ACTUAL trajectory, ballistic throw, pull-in, 1-3 wobbles with rising tension, catch or break-out. Three independent RNG streams so adding a spark to the trail cannot change who gets caught.

Firearms with GTA's specific feel: aim as a state with an asymmetric 0.2s in / 0.45s out ramp, spread as a live number the reticle IS rather than a cosmetic bloom, recoil as two springs plus a leaky residual applied to the ROUND and not just the picture, phased interruptible reload, surface-aware impacts.

Loadout system: absolute slots 1-4 rather than a cycle, because a cycle key is miserable when one of four items is a weapon you did not mean to raise at a creature you were about to befriend. The swap is not instant and gates both consumers by construction.
Near field filled: the first 25 metres went from bare grass carpet to layered clumps, flowers and foreground detail.
gaps: Integration is still in flight: the aim camera, the HUD reticle and ammo readout, the audio cues and the creature stagger reaction all exist as contracts that nothing consumes yet.
No blind A/B has been run against r12 yet. The r11 build was identified 5 of 5 at confidence 5.

rounds.title: Cast shadows actually render
rounds.summary: A blind critic wrote: 'Nothing in any of the five in-dev frames casts a shadow onto anything else, and that single absence produces most of the other symptoms the critics keep re-describing.' It was right, and the cause was not one bug but four, each measured before and after. The instructive part is what it was NOT: the shadow map was enabled, 2048x2048, with a valid texture, a correctly-following target and 79 casters. Every piece of the configuration was right and the feature still did nothing.
improvements: Key/fill rebalanced. A shadow can only remove the key's contribution, and the unshadowed fill was out-contributing the key 2:1 on the ground (key removed 86.7 -> 63.4; fill removed 86.7 -> 36.6), capping any possible shadow at a quarter of the meadow. Key share 0.27 -> 0.372.

Sun arc flattened from 63 deg/^1.6 to 48 deg/^1.0. Four of five daylight shots had been lit from 33-51 deg, where a 12 m tree's 10 m shadow hides under its own canopy. Golden hour now lands in the 18-25 deg band.

Sun azimuth rotated 67 deg off the world's composition axis. Measured angle between camera forward and the sun had been 172.9 / 179.1 / 172.7 on three daylight shots — lit from behind the lens, which throws every shadow behind the object casting it.

Shadow frustum widened and the light pushed back to 620 m. A 144 m box at a 51 deg key covers 93 m of ground; the tree-covered hillside the critics kept naming sits at 150-300 m and had never been in the shadow map.

Terrain itself now casts (it never had), so ridges and banks lay their far sides into shade. Acne handled with a slope-scaled polygon offset via customDepthMaterial — shadow.bias is constant in depth and normalBias buys almost nothing at a grazing sun.
gaps: The diff is 0.773/255 against an 8/255 target. Proven by experiment to be a content problem, not a lighting one: shrinking the shadow box to 30 m, which puts every texel on the near field at 1.5 cm each, made it worse.
Grass casting was tried and measured as a null result. Recorded in the source rather than silently dropped.

critique.verdict: 5 of 5 identified as the in-dev build, every one at confidence 5. Art direction 1 of 5 to us.
critique.biggest_gap: 'Nothing in the in-dev world casts or receives light locally. Fix grounded shadowing and emissive light before anything else.' Ranked first of four, ahead of atmospheric depth, terrain material variety, and untextured props at focal points.
critique.praise: 'The HUD is commercial quality, full stop. This is the one layer I genuinely could not have distinguished from a shipped product, and it's better designed than the UI in a lot of released games.' Also praised: creature silhouettes and shared shape language, colour restraint ('a disciplined yellow-green to blue-green range' — 'harder than it looks'), and shot-making instinct on the vista and the creature group.
critique.note: Worth recording honestly: the critic explicitly declined to call the flat-shaded low-poly look a flaw — 'that's a legitimate style'. Its objection was that 'lighting is doing none of the work that a stylized renderer needs it to do. Style is a choice; missing light transport is a bug.'

rounds.title: Cast shadows — the one change
rounds.summary: A blind critic: 'Nothing in any of the five in-dev frames casts a shadow onto anything else, and that single absence produces most of the other symptoms the critics keep re-describing.' I had this evidence two rounds earlier — disabling shadows changed the image by 0.001 — and misread it as 'shadows render but are pure black', blaming a blob that turned out to be an unrelated colour-decode bug. Now measured properly and handed over with the ruled-out list.
improvements: Berry dead-end root-caused: gather reach was 2.6m from the CENTRE of a 2.7m-wide thicket, so 37 of 37 nodes went unharvested for an entire 309-second session while the HUD said 'press E at a bush'. Curve now recovers and ends at 7.
The bond is celebrated: an 11-second banner, a permanent TRAVELS WITH YOU roster line, a lap of honour, and the companion foraging berries for you afterwards.
Hint spam eliminated — 0 of 28 beats contain a repeated line, was four identical copies in one beat.
Species discovery repaced: 4 of 4 recorded in five minutes, was 2 of 4 all session.
All five daylight shots cleared the local-contrast threshold (5.09-7.33 vs reference 5.2-9.9).
AI props fixed: a double sRGB decode was crushing them to near-black — the second instance of that bug class in this project.
Harness hardened: screenshots allow 120s and retry once, after concurrent builder load discarded two otherwise-good verification runs.
gaps: Cast shadows still absent — the round's whole purpose

rounds.title: Close the loop economy; finish terrain detail
rounds.summary: Two builders. One closes the berry dead-end and makes the bond moment unmissable; the other finishes the terrain surface-detail work that was interrupted. The visual target is local contrast above 5.0 on every daylight shot without regressing the tonal work of rounds 7–9.
improvements: Creature contact shadows now render — they were measuring a delta of ~0 under creature feet against a 25-luma shadow under the player's.

The taming HUD now shows stage and cost-to-finish ('NOTICED ●○○○ · 3 berries to go') with a world-anchored marker that survives leaving prompt range — the playtest critic's single highest-leverage change.
A range gate stopped berries being thrown into empty grass, and the game now names where to restock.
AI destinations bound to real scene geometry via a new src/ai/props.js, so 'walking to the lookout rock' can refer to a rock that exists.

Playtest harness made honest and fair: it now runs by actual simulated time (309s, was 163s while claiming five minutes) and models a player who RESPONDS to the HUD rather than following a fixed script — which is the only fair way to test a HUD change.
With a responsive player the naive session now ends with a tamed companion, up from zero.

rounds.title: Four builders against three critic verdicts
rounds.summary: All three instruments reported and each named one highest-leverage change. Terrain material variety (blind critic + local-contrast measure agreed independently); taming legibility — surface the stage and the cost-to-finish where the mood word is now; bind AI destinations to real visible props so the good decisions reach the screen; and ground the creatures, which currently cast no shadow at all.
improvements: Six instrument bugs found BY the critics and fixed: capture --only wiped the round mid-review; shots were never actually isolated, so a taming leaked into the 'creatures left completely alone' strip; the motion strips could not frame what they graded; playtest --minutes 5 ran only 163 simulated seconds; one reference image was the comp for two shots; the group shot framed the player instead of the group.
Motion strips rebuilt: subject-tracking camera near creature eye height, plus a third strip sampling every 0.25s for the acceleration-ramp criterion that coarser sampling cannot show.

rounds.title: Terrain material variety — the change both instruments named
rounds.summary: The blind critic (no access to any metric) and the objective local-contrast measure independently landed on the same defect: the ground is one uniform olive value across 40–70% of every frame, and the grass billboards end at a fixed radius against an untextured backing plane. Round 8 is slope- and noise-blended multi-material terrain, plus the specific artifacts the critic named.
improvements: Blind A/B methodology fixed: pw_11 was being used as the comp for two different shots, so the critic spotted that both 'A' images were identical — knowing one was real gave away the other. Every shot now uses a distinct reference.

creature_group shot rewritten: it was staged with the gameplay camera, which frames the player, so the 'group shot' contained three forty-pixel blobs in the left third with 60% empty grass. It now finds the creature cluster and frames it at readable scale.
gaps: Playtest: 0 tamed in five minutes; the richest system in the build only ever renders into a JSON field

rounds.title: Fix the two measured dominant defects — both turned out to be real bugs
rounds.summary: Ground albedo and creature rendering, both diagnosed to root cause rather than tuned. Four compounding defects made the ground dark: a linear/sRGB colour-space error that multiplied terrain albedo by 0.36 before any light hit it; grass instance normals rotated near-horizontal by the inverse-transpose of a non-uniform blade scale; a dusk grade applying contrast around a pivot above the tone-mapped signal, driving every pixel negative; and wind amplitude in world metres laying blades over by 57 degrees. The creature was a blank sphere because src/creatures/index.js was still the STUB — all the real craft existed and was imported by nothing.
improvements: Ground/sky luminance ratio 0.31 → 0.66–0.88, inside the reference band on all four priority shots
Highlight clipping 3.25% → 0.00%
Dusk mean luminance 40.6 → 52.6, against the reference night frame's 50.7
Creatures now render with wool lobes, oversized dark-tipped ears, upright horns, and a drawn face with iris and specular dot — the reference brief realised

Guardrails corrected against the reference instead of invented: the colour-count band was wrong, and ground/sky ratio is a daylight-only number so night shots are exempt rather than permanently flagged
Portrait staging fixed: the camera was placed at the player's ground height, which buried it inside any rising terrain — now each object is staged against the ground it actually stands on
Capture API exposes scene internals and groundAt(), so diagnostics measure the scene instead of arguing about it
tools/measure.py added: ground/sky ratio, saturation, clipping, palette width and local contrast against the real reference
gaps: Local contrast is now the dominant measurable gap: 1.7–4.5 vs the reference 5.2–9.9
Blind A/B still 0/5 — the critic identified every frame, though the reasons shifted from gross exposure faults to specific material and composition problems

verdicts.note: closest to shipping; killed by a hard black blob artifact and flat-shaded wool with almost no terminator
best-lit shot, real cast shadow; three unblended horizontal bands across the midground
good compositional intent, empty midground, visible grass cutoff ring
did not contain its own subject — camera framed the player (since fixed)
hard-clipped rectangular starfield; night applied as a global multiply, no light actually contributes

rounds.title: Rendering pipeline iterations
rounds.summary: Five rounds chasing the washed-out image. Honest outcome: r04, r05 and r06 are within 1% of each other on every tonal statistic — the last three rounds did not measurably change the picture. That plateau is what prompted switching from adjective-driven briefs to measured targets with hypotheses pre-eliminated by experiment.
improvements: Overexposure from the earlier rounds was largely corrected — highlight clipping fell from 47% to 3.25%
Scene became genuinely content-rich: 8860 grass blades, 266 trees, 306 rocks, 14 creatures at 143–170 draw calls
gaps: Three consecutive rounds produced no measurable change — the defect was never actually localised, only guessed at
The real cause (ground albedo, not exposure or shadows) went unidentified until it was isolated by controlled experiment

rounds.title: Nine systems built in parallel, then integrated
rounds.summary: Nine builder agents with fresh context, each owning one disjoint system directory, each required to read the art-direction brief, look at the real reference screenshots, and verify against their own rendered output. Integration capture succeeded — but the blind A/B verdict was 0/5.
improvements: All nine systems built and integrated: world, sky, player, creatures, ai, interaction, ui, audio, post
Third-person framing, aerial perspective, HUD, creature nameplates and a working taming loop all present
gaps: Blind A/B 0/5 — every frame correctly identified as not the commercial game (overexposure, no shadow structure, flat grade, low detail)

verdicts.note: blown out, 47% clipped, zero shadow structure
creature reads as a smooth untextured blob (edge 1.9 vs 9.8)

rounds.title: Scaffold, capture harness, blind-A/B tooling
rounds.summary: Engine, system contracts and the deterministic capture harness. The first run silently screenshotted the loading overlay and still reported OK — fixed, and a frame probe now fails any capture that is blank, uniform, or still showing an overlay.
improvements: Fixed-timestep engine with a system registry; systems never import each other, so builder agents own disjoint directories without conflicts
Deterministic seeded RNG and noise — same seed always produces the same world, which is what makes round-over-round A/B meaningful
Headless capture harness driving the game through the same input path a human uses
Matched-shot protocol: 6 staged stills + 2 motion strips
Blind A/B pack builder that normalises resolution/format/quality so critics judge the picture, not a technical tell
17 official Palworld stills + 60 trailer frames acquired, curated, and readable by agents
gaps: Stub art across the board — this round only proved the measuring instruments work
